description:
The Government Grants Managed Service \(GGMS\) pilot is an end-to-end, technology-enabled managed service that seeks to deliver at least a 20% reduction in grant administration costs and significant improvements in data, through an innovative service design. The GGMS pilot has been operational since January 2024. Initially due to conclude 31 March 2025, but received approval to extend to 31 March 2026 by the Investment Committee, as a paid-for service for departments, ALBs and local authorities.

The GGMS has an innovative delivery model: operating model, processes, systems and data are owned by government. Only human resources for administration are outsourced and supplier\(s\) can therefore be changed easily. PwC are the current supplier for the pilot.

The GGMS uses an ecosystem of digital tools \(**GGIS, Find a Grant, Apply for a Grant, Spotlight**\) to facilitate the end-to-end delivery of grant schemes. This also includes the **Grant Lifecycle Utility \(GLU\)**: a working prototype solution \(Proof of Concept\) on MS Power Apps, which provides the case management, workflow, team management, scoring, and MI / reporting capabilities for grant administrators.

--

{color:rgb(0, 0, 0)/}The solution \(GLU - Grants Lifecycle Utility\) is a Microsoft based solution built to digitise and streamline the Grants Administration process for the Government Grants Managed Service. The solution is built using Microsoft Power Platform and encompasses a Model Driven Application, Power Automate Flows, Plug-ins and custom integrations with GGIS, Find & Apply and Google Drive.  
  
The solution in essence acts as a case management solution for the set up and execution of Government Grant Schemes and the associated management and assessment of all applications that are submitted under this scheme.  
  
When a scheme is set up, the department provides the GGIS Reference Number \(Scheme ID\) to the GGMS and the scheme is then set up in GLU, working through the required stages within the Business Process Flow to ensure set up is done correctly.  
  
Following the set up, applications are then pulled into GLU via the Find & Apply API. Once received in GLU, any documents submitted as part of the applicant's submission are pushed into a secure Google Drive folder using Microsoft's Google Drive connector. The application will then proceed through 4 core processes: Assessment, Outcome, Award and Monitoring \(depending on the success\).{color}

{color:rgb(4, 5, 6)/}NB: Discovery underway into possible API integration between Find/Apply and Glu \(two way sync\){color}
name: Grants Lifecycle Utility (GLU)

## Supplier Profile: Jaggaer Ltd

**Key Details**

*   **Supplier:** Jaggaer Ltd

*   **Contract End Date:** 31 March 2028

*   **Contract Tier:** Gold

### System Overview

The Jaggaer eSourcing Portal is a website and sourcing platform that enables users to create commercial agreements for procurement purposes. Customers can use the platform to select relevant suppliers and commercial agreements.

### Core Functions

**1\. Internal Operations \(CCS\)**

*   **Regulated Procurements:** Provides functionality to conduct "above threshold" regulated procurements \(i.e., "OJEU" level\) to create new CCS commercial agreements.

*   **Assisted Procurement:** Facilitates "call-off" and "open market" procurements for customer requirements managed via the CCS "assisted procurement" service.

**2\. Customer-Facing \(Self-Service\)**

*   **Call-Off Activity:** Offers a "free to use" self-service portal for customers to execute call-offs from most CCS commercial frameworks.

*   **Support:** Buyers and suppliers are supported through comprehensive guidance, regular webinars, and assistance from the internal eEnablement Team.

### Modules & Capabilities

*   **Sourcing:** Core eSourcing functionalities.

*   **Award:** Awarding functionality, potentially utilizing an API that pulls through from Jaggaer \(Commerce Decisions\).

*   **Contract Management:** Includes contract management modules and "Contract \+".

*   **Self-Serve:** Dedicated functions enabling customers to manage framework call-offs independently.

Hosts all procurement documentation including guidance, processes, SOPs etc as well central teams processes including CAAAB and ICMT

[Knowledge Centre](https://sites.google.com/a/crowncommercial.gov.uk/delivery-assurance/home "https://sites.google.com/a/crowncommercial.gov.uk/delivery-assurance/home") is a central repository for directorates and teams to share what they do, their standard operating procedures \(SOPs\), related templates, guidance, documentation, processes, useful information and other knowledge sources. It is a key tool to support GCA staff carrying out their day to day duties and to locate business information.

The main purpose of the Knowledge Centre is to share operational knowledge and information between teams, directorates and the wider GCA organisation. The centre was originally built for Proc Ops to use and store all their key documentation.

The service is provisioned and hosted by the Cabinet Office as part of the Google suite.The Knowledge Centre is governed by the GCA KIM team who are responsible for the overall structure, defining the standards and carrying out the quality audits. The Knowledge Centre page content is created, edited and approved by the directorates, this provides the flexibility for directorates to update and publish operational information within their own directorate approval channels.

This solution provides GCA with:

*   A central repository for CCS enterprise, directorate and team Standard Operating Procedures \(SOPs\), internal processes, including relevant templates, guidance, service request forms and documentation.

*   Links to relevant sites and other sources of useful information.

*   The ability to manage the standardisation of all GCA Knowledge Centre Pages.

*   A location to provide training documentation to Directorates/New Knowledge Centre Editors on how to create and update new content.

The Content within the Knowledge Centre Pages is owned by the Directorate Information Asset Owners \(IAOs\) \(SCSs\).

KIM expertise \(Knowledge and Information Management\) is required to operate this service.

[https://sites.google.com/a/crowncommercial.gov.uk/delivery-assurance/home](https://sites.google.com/a/crowncommercial.gov.uk/delivery-assurance/home)
